audits.title: AN AUDIT OF PAEDIATRIC VANCOMYCIN DOSING
audits.standard: Local paediatric vancomycin guideline: 100% correct starting dose, 90% levels at correct time, 80% third-dose troughs in range (10–15 mg/L), 90% appropriate action for out-of-range levels

cycle1.result: 100% correct starting dose; 90% of levels taken at the correct time; 33% of initial levels in range (a further 31% after dose change); 93% appropriate actions; three of six standards met.

audits.intervention: Suggested changing dosing frequency to four times a day or continuous infusion.
audits.other_findings: Two standards could not be assessed as no neonates or renal impairment cases; 62 levels reviewed.
audits.citation: Mohsin-Shaikh S, Lumb P. AN AUDIT OF PAEDIATRIC VANCOMYCIN DOSING. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2016;101(9):e2.2-e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.10.

audits.title: AN AUDIT OF VANCOMYCIN PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS WHEN VANCOMYCIN IS ADMINISTERED BY CONTINUOUS INTRAVENOUS INFUSION IN NEONATES

cycle1.result: 28% of concentrations within the therapeutic range.

audits.intervention: Switch to continuous intravenous vancomycin infusion (loading dose 15 mg/kg then 20-50 mg/kg/day by creatinine and corrected gestational age), based on another hospital's regimen.

cycle2.result: 62% of 115 concentrations within range (60.8% first, 60% second, 65.6% subsequent); 71.3% within a 10% widened range.

audits.other_findings: Comparator hospital achieved 77%; doses were prepared on the ward without aseptic facilities. Prefilled syringes and re-audit recommended.
audits.citation: Whitticase L, Holder G, Cawsey M, Bedford-Russell A. AN AUDIT OF VANCOMYCIN PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS WHEN VANCOMYCIN IS ADMINISTERED BY CONTINUOUS INTRAVENOUS INFUSION IN NEONATES. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2016;101(9):e2.52-e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.56.

audits.title: P02 An audit of vancomycin dosing in the neonatal units

cycle1.result: Correct initial dose 28/28 (100%); level taken at correct time 13/15 (87%); 19/31 levels (62%) within 10–20 mg/L; all 6 levels >20 mg/L had next dose held, but follow-up adjustment often suboptimal; 3 of 4 low levels not acted on.

audits.intervention: Guideline amended (single safe range 10–20 mg/L, doses adjusted on levels not age) and teaching sessions with worked examples planned for prescribers and nurses.
audits.other_findings: 19 patients had 28 courses and 31 levels. Levels appeared to be interpreted in isolation, causing avoidable repeat high levels.
audits.citation: Penny F, Shruti P. P02 An audit of vancomycin dosing in the neonatal units. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2018;103(2):e1.5-e1. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.13.

audits.title: P39 Continuous vancomycin dosing: an audit and evaluation
audits.standard: Local vancomycin prescribing and therapeutic drug monitoring guidance

cycle1.result: Loading, initial continuous dosing and TDM generally in line with local guidelines; 9% of first levels subtherapeutic; of 298 levels 56% therapeutic, 19% supratherapeutic, 25% subtherapeutic

audits.other_findings: A previous audit of intermittent dosing found 50% of first levels subtherapeutic; no vancomycin-specific adverse effects.
audits.citation: Fiona R, Rachel W, Mildrid Y. P39 Continuous vancomycin dosing: an audit and evaluation. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2018;103(2):e1.43-e1. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.48.

audits.title: P003 Intermittent vancomycin in paediatrics: implementation and audit of a new guideline
audits.standard: Trust intermittent IV vancomycin guideline (2016) with loading dose and increased dose and frequency versus BNFC
audits.setting: Paediatric wards (patients ≥1 month) on intermittent IV vancomycin

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation audit: 7% of levels in therapeutic range at 48 hours; lack of support for appropriate dosing and monitoring.

audits.intervention: New trust guideline for intermittent IV vancomycin (loading dose, higher dose and frequency) with pharmacist intervention.

cycle2.result: Loading dose used appropriately in 83%; levels at correct times in 90%; 40% in range at 48 hours; 100% reviewed at 48 hours; out-of-range levels reviewed per guideline in 40%, rising to 80% with pharmacist intervention.

audits.other_findings: 30% still needed dose adjustment at 48 hours. Authors plan for pharmacist prescribers to adjust treatment directly.
audits.citation: Gray J. P003 Intermittent vancomycin in paediatrics: implementation and audit of a new guideline. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2019;104(7):e2.5-e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.13.

audits.title: P15 Two-cycle audit on paediatric vancomycin prescribing and monitoring: tertiary centre experience
audits.standard: Local trust guideline (2018) for intravenous vancomycin in children
audits.setting: Tertiary centre; paediatric patients (>30 days and <17 years) receiving intravenous vancomycin

cycle1.result: Correct frequency 75.9%; correct first dose 58.6%; concentrations taken at correct time 89.7%; therapeutic first concentration 24.1% (70.4% under range); second concentration in range 61.9%.

audits.intervention: Significant changes to electronic prescription and concentration report templates; guideline recirculated to all paediatric prescribers.

cycle2.result: Correct frequency 92.6%; correct first dose 71.4%; concentrations taken at correct time 96.2%; therapeutic first concentration 19.2% (65.4% under range); second concentration in range 57.9%.

audits.other_findings: Non-compliance with prescribing was due to prescribers following BNFC rather than trust guidance. Therapeutic concentrations were still not achieved in over 80% of patients, prompting a call to re-evaluate the dosing guideline.
audits.citation: Chin M, Williams E. P15 Two-cycle audit on paediatric vancomycin prescribing and monitoring: tertiary centre experience. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2023;108(5):8.2-9. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.14.
